messages:
support_jen: customer escalated CS-2298 - intermittent 401s around 2026-03-09T14:10Z. Errors include 'invalid signature' and 'kid not found'. They say it started right after an IdP key rotation.

ali_platform: can you share the raw Authorization header and gateway logs? is this their hosted IdP or our hosted OIDC?

support_jen: their IdP (login.authco.com). Sample header: `Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6InJvdF8yMDI2MDMwIn0...` Gateway log:
```
2026-03-09T14:11:58Z gateway token_validation.go:87 error="jwks: kid not found"
2026-03-09T14:11:59Z gateway token_validation.go:109 error="jwt: invalid signature"
```

maya_ops: config change landed at 2026-03-09T14:11:05Z: jwks_cache_ttl set from 600s -> 300s (deploy-bot shows infra-release committed). could be related to more frequent refreshes exposing race windows.

tomas_sec: our JWKS cache is TTL-based (5m fallback to redis). currently on kid-miss we fail. we should try immediate refetch on kid-miss and retry once. also add 60s leeway on exp/nbf to tolerate clock skew.

ali_platform: agreed. also ensure we key the JWKS store by (kid, alg) not just kid. we saw cases where two different alg families share a kid string during IdP migrations.

sara_support: repro steps sent to customer: 1) curl -I https://login.authco.com/.well-known/jwks.json 2) check if new kid present 3) compare kid in token header to jwks response. they replied new kid appears after ~90s. intermittent failures lasted ~2m.

ali_platform: suggested pseudo patch: `on kid-miss -> force refresh JWKS once -> if still missing -> fail. validate alg matches allowed algs (RS256/ES256) and enforce (kid,alg) lookup. add leeway=60s for claims.`

infra-release: canary plan: push jwks-refetch patch to us-east-1 at 2026-03-09T15:00Z. will monitor refetch metrics.

deploy-bot: Deployment started: jwks-refetch-canary -> us-east-1 by @ali_platform at 2026-03-09T15:00:00Z

ops_oncall: seeing a burst of refetches after canary but success rate ~98%. no downstream 500s.

support_jen: customer confirms 401s stopped after 15:05Z. they admitted their migration rotated keys rapidly and didn't serve old keys consistently. advised them to keep old keys available for a reasonable TTL.

tomas_sec: follow-ups: open infra ticket to add unit tests for rotation race, implement (kid,alg) mapping, emit metrics: jwks_kid_miss, jwks_refetch_success, jwks_kid_alg_mismatch. log refetch events with node id.

sara_support: updating CS-2298 with timeline, mitigation, and customer guidance. will keep platform fix as blocking work until backported.

maya_ops: consider reverting TTL change? longer TTL reduces sensitivity to spurious rotations but delays legitimate key updates. prefer short TTL + fetch-on-miss.

infra-release: canary complete at 2026-03-09T15:03:00Z, rolling to more regions pending signoff.

support_jen: marking ticket resolved by customer; leaving platform follow-up open. thanks everyone.
